'''Laura Otis''' is a Professor of English at [[Emory University]] who works on literature and science.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.english.emory.edu/people/faculty/otis.htm |title=Laura Otis: Professor |website=emory.edu |accessdate=2010-04-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100409073039/http://english.emory.edu/people/faculty/otis.htm |archivedate=2010-04-09 }}</ref>

She graduated from [[Yale University]] with a B.S. in Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry in 1983, and from the [[University of California, San Francisco]] with an M.A. in Neuroscience in 1988, and from [[Cornell University]] with a Ph.D. in Comparative Literature in 1991.

She was a guest scholar at the [[Max Planck Institute]] for the History of Science.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.phf.upenn.edu/09-10/otis.shtml |title=Reconnecting Visual and Verbal Thinking |first=Laura |last=Otis |website=Penn Humanities Forum |date=19 February 2010 |accessdate=2010-04-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100618224645/http://www.phf.upenn.edu/09-10/otis.shtml |archivedate=2010-06-18 }}</ref>
